posts.text:
如果代码库里的每个文件都能自己解释、自己修改，还会提醒相关文件「你也得改」，Coding Agent 会不会更稳？

UIUC 和 Penn State 这篇论文提出 HERMES，把代码库里的文件、配置和测试变成一个个 Dev-Primitive。

可以把它理解成：每个组件旁边都有一个专门理解它的小 Agent。

遇到任务时，HERMES 先沿依赖关系找到真正相关的组件，只激活这一小部分。它们各自修改自己负责的内容，同时同步接口变化、配置约束和测试要求。

如果执行失败，系统会根据报错和测试结果，只重新激活相关组件继续修，不需要每轮重新读完整个仓库。

论文在 SWE-bench、仓库级重构、Terminal-Bench 和 DevOps 四类任务上测试，平均提升 12.4 个百分点。

还有就是把内部组件 Agent 换成 Qwen3-8B，整体只比全 GPT-5.6 Sol 方案低约 4.5 个百分点；在 Terminal-Bench 上成本还能下降 26.2%。

面对大仓库里的 Coding Agent，可能更需要一套稳定的「局部理解 + 协作修改 + 失败后定点修复」机制。

Harness 的价值也像是在组织代码、上下文和 Agent 之间的信息流。

quotedTweet.text:
whoever built this realized we've been using our smartest AI for the dumbest possible jobs

your $20-$200/mo frontier model is researching, writing code, planning…

and then you're paying that same brain to decide YES / NO.

Jev flips that.

it's a tiny decision model that sits in front of the expensive stuff and takes the boring forks:

-> which agent goes next?
-> is this worth researching?
-> reply or ignore?
-> publish, wait or escalate?
-> BUY / SELL / HOLD?
-> click this or keep looking?

then I saw the numbers people are posting and the whole architecture started making a lot more sense.

~1,000 papers classified for around $0.08
~500 emails sorted for around $0.035

browser-agent loops shown at around 7 seconds for ~$0.0039

and at the quoted pricing, roughly 10,000 ~1K-token decisions comes out around $0.42.

that's not because Jev got smarter than Claude.

it's because nobody asked it to be Claude.

the setup is stupidly simple:

-> big LLM gets the hard thinking, research and writing
-> Jev gets the thousands of tiny decisions between those steps
-> code actually clicks, saves, sends and runs

and suddenly you start seeing these little decisions everywhere.

> your inbox.
> X feed.
> support queue.
> meetings.
> leads.
> video clips.
> browser agents.
> even paper-trading loops.

that's the part I think most agent builders are missing.

the expensive model doesn't need to touch every step just because it's able to touch every step.

> let Claude think.
> let Jev decide what deserves Claude.
> let code do the actual work.

I broke down how to wire Jev into your agent + the exact router setup in the article below
quotedTweet.translationZh:
做出这个东西的人意识到，我们一直在用最聪明的 AI 做最蠢的工作。

你每月花 $20-$200 买的前沿模型，在做研究、写代码、做规划……

然后你还在花钱让同一个大脑来判断 YES / NO。

Jev 把这件事反过来了。

它是一个微型决策模型，放在昂贵模型前面，处理那些无聊的分岔：

-> 下一个该哪个 agent 上？
-> 这件事值得研究吗？
-> 回复还是忽略？
-> 发布、等待还是升级处理？
-> BUY / SELL / HOLD？
-> 点这个，还是继续找？

后来我看到大家发出来的数据，整个架构就突然合理多了。

约 1,000 篇论文分类，成本大约 $0.08
约 500 封邮件整理，成本大约 $0.035

浏览器 agent 循环约 7 秒，成本约 $0.0039

按公开报价算，大约 10,000 次约 1K token 的决策，成本约 $0.42。

这不是因为 Jev 比 Claude 更聪明。

而是因为没人要求它成为 Claude。

这个设置简单得离谱：

-> 大 LLM 负责困难的思考、研究和写作
-> Jev 负责这些步骤之间成千上万个微小决策
-> 代码真正去点击、保存、发送和运行

然后你会突然发现，这些小决策无处不在。

> 你的收件箱。
> X 信息流。
> 支持队列。
> 会议。
> 销售线索。
> 视频片段。
> 浏览器 agents。
> 甚至模拟交易循环。

我觉得这正是大多数 agent 构建者漏掉的部分。

昂贵模型没必要因为能参与每一步，就真的参与每一步。

> 让 Claude 思考。
> 让 Jev 判断什么值得交给 Claude。
> 让代码完成实际工作。

quotedTweet.text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
关于经济中的智能体，我一直在琢磨一些零散想法：

• 从某种意义上说，公司是最早的超级智能。它们常常能利用摊销后的认知盈余，推进自身利益，哪怕这会损害某些消费者：相对于公司的优化能力，消费者可能注意力不足、信息不足、不够理性，等等。（比如预订流程最后常见的一些经典保险加购，价格通常明显高于普通保单。）Herbert Simon 提出了有限理性的概念，而企业往往会从中受益。多亏个人智能体，我们在与公司打交道时可能会变得更理性一些。

• 结果究竟会如何变化？某些价格歧视会变得不那么有效（如果每个智能体都认真搜寻优惠券，优惠券还怎么运作？），某些客户交叉补贴也会改变（今天，忘记取消订阅的人补贴了那些不会忘的人）。从整个经济来看，我还不确定这些变化最终会落到谁身上。

• 在公司战略中，人们长期争论渠道和产品质量哪个更重要。也许你做出了更好的东西，但有人知道吗？人们难道不会继续购买 ACME Corp Mousetraps 吗？我认为，个人智能体会成为一种偏向产品质量的结构性补贴。如果个人在每次购买前都至少花 10 小时做研究，市场会有什么不同？在边际上，我认为专注于把产品做得更好，会成为公司更有效的策略。这是好事！

• 如果这是真的，一个推论是，关于产品质量的信息会变得更加重要、更有影响力。今天，大多数人聚合和整合这类数据的能力非常有限，但智能体会对这类信号有无止境的渴求。（人们常说数据正变得更有价值，因为它有助于模型训练。这当然没错，但我认为还有另一种次级方式：数据作为更廉价智能的补充，本身也会变得更有价值。）

• 一个大问题是，智能体会增强超级明星效应（理性的智能体都选择同一个产品），还是增加分散度（因为每个人都有略微不同的品味和偏好，而智能体善于挖掘这些偏好，最终克服我们一直被迫接受的人为聚类）。

• 许多互联网公司通过需求路由变现，而这往往又建立在注意力短暂之上。“我会点击我看到的第一个东西。”这带来了一定程度的低效，因为公司试图讨好反复无常的排名算法，并承担各种展示位费用。这并不全是无谓损失（支付意愿本身也是一种信号，对买家有价值），但并不理想。在个人智能体的世界里，这种路由的性质和价值会如何变化？我不知道答案，但我认为影响可能会相当大。

• 我写的许多内容都建立在一个假设之上：个人智能体会站在消费者一边。我怀疑这会是胜出的策略，但它是否为真，以及“为真”意味着什么，还牵涉许多其他问题。

总体来看，市场是一台大规模并行、去中心化且高度不完美的价值归因机器；综合所有影响来看，我觉得产品质量这一点很可能是最重要的：智能体会改变反向传播的性质，让更好产品获得更高回报。也许这太乐观了，但我怀疑（也希望）那些做出自己引以为豪之物的公司，会感觉宇宙稍微更偏向它们一些。

如果代码库里的每个文件都能自己解释、自己修改，还会提醒相关文件「你也得改」，Coding Agent 会不会更稳？

UIUC 和 Penn State 这篇论文提出 HERMES，把代码库里的文件、配置和测试变成一个个 Dev-Primitive。

可以把它理解成：每个组件旁边都有一个专门理解它的小 Agent。

遇到任务时，HERMES 先沿依赖关系找到真正相关的组件，只激活这一小部分。它们各自修改自己负责的内容，同时同步接口变化、配置约束和测试要求。

如果执行失败，系统会根据报错和测试结果，只重新激活相关组件继续修，不需要每轮重新读完整个仓库。

论文在 SWE-bench、仓库级重构、Terminal-Bench 和 DevOps 四类任务上测试，平均提升 12.4 个百分点。

还有就是把内部组件 Agent 换成 Qwen3-8B，整体只比全 GPT-5.6 Sol 方案低约 4.5 个百分点；在 Terminal-Bench 上成本还能下降 26.2%。

面对大仓库里的 Coding Agent，可能更需要一套稳定的「局部理解 + 协作修改 + 失败后定点修复」机制。

Harness 的价值也像是在组织代码、上下文和 Agent 之间的信息流。

一个 Coding Agent，现在已经可以一次改上千个 PR 了。

Block 最近公开了他们怎么用 Claude Fable 5 做公司级代码迁移。

一次任务可以跨多个 Repo、几百万行代码。Fable 负责高层规划和拆解，再把具体改文件、跑测试这些工作分给更便宜的模型。

有意思的是人类工程师的角色也在往上移。

架构、数据模型、API 和关键设计决策留给人，机械修改和大规模迁移越来越多交给 Agent。Block 甚至已经让 Agent 定期扫描百万行级代码库，持续清理技术债。

所以当 Agent 开始能组织和维护整个代码库，Coding Agent 就越像一支软件团队，而不只是一个会写代码的助手。

Recently had the chance to interview @benhylak on how he is thinking about simulations in our AI Evals Course 😁

Simulations are incredibly useful for evals when you  do them well.  Ben discusses what he learned from implementing simulations for evals at several companies.  Some fun topics came up, my favorite being "simulation awareness" - when models know they are in a simulation.  

Below is a chapter summary:

02:02 Why input/output tests miss agent failures
10:59 Replay production traces to see what a change breaks
13:18 Recreate the data and tools around the agent
16:27 How agents detect simulations and change their behavior
20:39 Choose scenarios that test the change you made
22:00 Check answers, costs, and tool behavior across runs
26:43 Replay known failures to verify a fix
31:20 Common mistakes that make simulations misleading
32:20 Check that the simulation reproduces production behavior
37:37 When to start using simulations

You can also watch on YT here: https://t.co/EjlKZMw2y1
